'''Colin Lingwood Mallows''' (10 September 1930 – 4 November 2023) was an English statistician who worked in the United States from 1960.<ref>{{cite book|author=Upton, Graham|author2=Cook, Ian|title=A Dictionary of Statistics|edition=3rd|publisher=Oxford University Press|chapter=Mallows, Colin L.|date=13 March 2014|page=252|isbn=9780191044632|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=P-CrBwAAQBAJ&pg=PA252}}</ref> He was known for [[Mallows's Cp|Mallows's ''C<sub>p</sub>'']], a regression model diagnostic procedure, widely used in [[regression analysis]] and the [[Fowlkes–Mallows index]], a popular [[Cluster analysis|clustering]] validation criterion.<ref name=Interview>{{cite journal|title=A conversation with Colin L. Mallows|author=Denby, Lorraine|author-link=Lorraine Denby|author2=Landwehr, Jim|journal=International Statistical Review|year=2013|volume=81|issue=3|pages=338–360|url=http://www.mh-data.com/uploads/3/6/5/4/3654893/mallows-interview.pdf|doi=10.1111/insr.12038|s2cid=119937742}}</ref><ref name=jrrs>{{Cite journal |last=Dalal |first=Siddhartha |last2=Landwehr |first2=James |date=12 April 2024 |title=Colin Lingwood Mallows: a great ambidextrous statistician, 1930–2023 |url=https://academic.oup.com/jrsssa/article/187/2/553/7486387 |journal=Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series A: Statistics in Society |language=en |volume=187 |issue=2 |pages=553–554 |doi=10.1093/jrsssa/qnad141 |issn=0964-1998}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Mallows began studying at [[University College London]] (UCL) in 1948 and received in 1951 his bachelor's degree and in 1953 his PhD (at the age of 22) from  under [[Florence Nightingale David]] and [[Norman Lloyd Johnson]] with thesis ''Some problems connected with distribution problems.''<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=42266|title=Colin L. Mallows}}</ref> Mallows joined the UCL faculty and taught there from 1955 to 1959 with a sabbatical year at [[Princeton University]] in the academic year 1957–1958. He worked for [[Bell Labs]] in [[Murray Hill, New Jersey]] from 1960 to 1995 and then for [[AT&T Labs]] in [[Florham Park, New Jersey]] from 1995 to 2000, when he retired. From 2000, Mallows was a consultant for [[Avaya|Avaya Labs]]. He was the author or coauthor of about 140 research publications.<ref name=Interview/>

== Death ==
Mallows died on 4 November 2023, at the age of 93.<ref name=obit>{{cite web |title=Obituary: Colin Mallows 1930–2023 |url=https://imstat.org/2023/12/15/obituary-colin-mallows-1930-2023/ |website=Institute of Mathematical Statistics |access-date=28 December 2023 |date=15 December 2023}}</ref><ref name=wright></ref>

== Honors and awards ==
Mallows was awarded the [[R. A. Fisher Lectureship]] in 1997, the [[Deming Lectureship]] in 2004, and the [[Wilks Memorial Award]] in 2007. Mallows and [[George Box]] are the only two statisticians to have received all three of those honours.<ref name=Interview/> He was a Fellow of the American Statistical Association, the Institute of Mathematical Statistics, and the Royal Statistical Society.<ref name=obit/>

Mallows solved a $10,000 mathematical problem posed by [[John Horton Conway]],<ref>{{cite book|author=Pickover, Clifford A.|chapter=The crying of fractal batrachian 1,489|title=''In:'' Chaos and Fractals|pages=127–131|year=1998|isbn=9780080528861|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=A51ARsapVuUC&pg=PA127}}</ref> but declined the prize money on the grounds that the problem was too easy.<ref name=Interview/>

== Selected publications ==
*"Generalizations of Tchebycheff's inequalities." Journal of the Royal Statistical Society. Series B (Methodological) (1956): 139–176. {{JSTOR|2983702?}}
*with David E. Barton: "The randomization bases of the problem of the amalgamation of weighted means." Journal of the Royal Statistical Society. Series B (Methodological) (1961): 423–433. {{JSTOR|2984032}}
*[https://academic.oup.com/biomet/article-abstract/48/1-2/133/225731 "Latent vectors of random symmetric matrices."] Biometrika 48, no. 1–2 (1961): 133–149. {{doi|10.1093/biomet/48.1-2.133}}
*with D. E. Barton: "Some aspects of the random sequence." The Annals of Mathematical Statistics (1965): 236–260. {{JSTOR|2238090}}
*"An even simpler proof of Opal's inequality." Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 16 (1965):  173. {{doi|10.1090/S0002-9939-1965-0170989-6}}
*with H. L. Frisch and F. A. Bovey. "On the stereoregularity of vinyl polymer chains." The Journal of Chemical Physics 45, no. 5 (1966): 1565–1577. {{doi|10.1063/1.1727800}}
*with John Riordan: "The inversion enumerator for labeled trees." Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 74 (1968): 92–94. {{doi|10.1090/S0002-9904-1968-11888-9}}
*With William H. Williams: "Systematic biases in panel surveys due to differential nonresponse." Journal of the American Statistical Association 65, no. 331 (1970): 1338–1349. {{doi|10.1080/01621459.1970.10481169}}
*with David F. Andrews: "Scale mixtures of normal distributions." Journal of the Royal Statistical Society. Series B (Methodological) (1974): 99–102. {{JSTOR|2984774 }}
*with John M. Chambers and B. W. Stuck: "A method for simulating stable random variables." Journal of the American Statistical Association 71, no. 354 (1976): 340–344. {{doi|10.1080/01621459.1976.10480344}}
*"Robust methods—some examples of their use." The American Statistician 33, no. 4 (1979): 179–184. {{doi|10.1080/00031305.1979.10482689}}
*with Edward B. Fowlkes: "A method for comparing two hierarchical clusterings." Journal of the American Statistical Association 78, no. 383 (1983): 553–569. {{doi|10.1080/01621459.1983.10478008}}
*with Siddharta R. Dalal: "When should one stop testing software?." Journal of the American Statistical Association 83, no. 403 (1988): 872–879. {{doi|10.1080/01621459.1988.10478676}}
*with David Draper, James S. Hodges, and Daryl Pregibon: "Exchangeability and data analysis." Journal of the Royal Statistical Society. Series A (Statistics in Society) (1993): 9–37. {{JSTOR|2982858}}
*with S. R. Dalal: "Factor-covering designs for testing software." Technometrics 40, no. 3 (1998): 234–243. {{doi|10.1080/00401706.1998.10485524}}
*[[Lorraine Denby]], James M. Landwehr, Jean Meloche, John Tuck, Bowei Xi, George Michailidis, and Vijayan N. Nair: "Statistical aspects of the analysis of data networks." Technometrics 49, no. 3 (2007): 318–334. {{doi|10.1198/004017007000000290}}
